title: Bacteria: tiny living things
examples: Are all bacteria bad for us?
What is the difference between useful and harmful bacteria?

explain.say: Today we are learning about bacteria, which are very tiny living things. They are too small to see without special equipment.
One way bacteria reproduce is through a process called binary fission. This means the cell splits into two equal halves.
When bacteria reproduce this way, they are doubling very quickly. This rapid doubling is how their numbers grow so fast.
Some bacteria are useful to us in many ways. For example, some help us digest our food in our gut.
However, some bacteria can be harmful and cause infections. These are sometimes called pathogens. We must learn to keep them away.
Think about making yogurt. Bacteria are used to change milk into that tasty, creamy substance. This is a real-life use.

faq.q: Do all bacteria make us sick?
faq.a: No, many bacteria are actually helpful to us. They live in our bodies and help us digest food properly. You could also ask if all bacteria are germs, or what bacteria are good for us?

They can multiply very fast through a process called binary fission. This means one cell splits into two, and then those two split into four, and so on. You might also ask about bacterial growth rates, or how fast germs multiply?

faq.q: What is the difference between useful and harmful bacteria?
faq.a: Useful bacteria help us in everyday life, like in making food. Harmful bacteria are the ones that can cause infections or make us feel unwell. You could also ask for examples of beneficial bacteria, or what germs cause sickness?

Binary fission is the method bacteria use to reproduce. It is simply the process where one cell divides into two identical new cells. You could ask how bacteria reproduce, or what the splitting process is?
asks: What is the splitting process for bacteria?

faq.a: Yes, bacteria are living organisms. They are single-celled and carry out all the life processes needed to survive. You could also ask if bacteria are alive, or what bacteria need to live?

facts: Bacteria are single-celled organisms, meaning they are made of only one cell.
Binary fission is the asexual method by which bacteria reproduce.
Some bacteria are beneficial and help with digestion, like those in yogurt.
Harmful bacteria are often called pathogens because they cause disease.

quiz.say: Bacteria reproduce by splitting into two identical cells. This process is called:
quiz.why: This is the specific term for how bacteria divide into two new cells.

wrong.0: Mitosis is used by larger, complex cells, not single bacteria.
wrong.1: Budding is a method used by some fungi, not typically bacteria.
wrong.2: Meiosis is related to sexual reproduction in complex life forms.

quiz.say: If a bacterium doubles every twenty minutes, how many will there be in one hour?
quiz.why: In one hour, the bacteria will double three times: 1 to 2, 2 to 4, and 4 to 8.

wrong.0: This is too high; the growth is exponential, not linear.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because doubling means multiplying by two each time.
wrong.3: This suggests adding two each time, not multiplying by two.

quiz.say: Which type of bacteria is responsible for helping us digest food?
quiz.why: Beneficial bacteria are those that perform helpful functions in our bodies, like digestion.

wrong.1: Pathogens are the ones that cause illness, not help digestion.
wrong.2: Microbes is a general term for tiny life, not a classification of use.
wrong.3: This is too general; we need to know if they are helpful or harmful.
